findings.problem: `finiteVectorDensity` has no simp or apply lemma. Every user has to unfold the definition and rebuild the same rewrite chain by hand: `Submodule.coe_sum`, `Submodule.coe_smul`, `sum_apply`, `smul_apply`. Here the chain also unfolds `finiteOperatorCoefficient` and then uses `operatorCoefficient_apply`. That bypasses the existing `@[simp]` lemma `finiteOperatorCoefficient_apply`. The same unfolding recurs in `FiniteVectorDensityTensor.lean` (lines 35 and 58) and, with `Function.comp_apply`, in `HypertraceFiniteDensity.lean` (line 180). So the definition's simp normal form is missing, and each proof leaks the definition's internal structure (a `Submodule` sum of `finiteOperatorCoefficient`s).
findings.proposed_change: Next to `finiteVectorDensity` in `HypertraceFiniteDensity.lean`, add a lemma and mark it `@[simp]`: `(finiteVectorDensity w x).val T = ∑ k, (w k : ℂ) * ∑ i, inner ℂ (x k) (T (x k))`. Here the inner sum is the one-term sum from `finiteOperatorCoefficient_apply` with `ι = Unit`, or better a single `inner ℂ (x k) (T (x k))`. Prove it once using `Submodule.coe_sum`, `Submodule.coe_smul`, `sum_apply`, `smul_apply` and `finiteOperatorCoefficient_apply`. Then reduce line 27 to something like `simp only [finiteVectorDensity_apply, Complex.re_sum, Complex.re_ofReal_mul]` (or plain `simp`). Replace the matching `simp only`/`simpa` lists in `FiniteVectorDensityTensor.lean` lines 35 and 58 the same way. Stating the lemma with `finiteVectorDensity` kept folded gives the intended normal form: an evaluation of the density is a weighted sum of vector-state expectations.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical rewrite for evaluating a finite vector density. Proofs no longer unfold the `Submodule` structure or `finiteOperatorCoefficient` (which skips the existing simp lemma `finiteOperatorCoefficient_apply`). Changing the definition of `finiteVectorDensity` later would then touch one lemma, not three or more proofs across files.
